report_html:
No Fixed Address

JAX throw by design. They pass -1% over expectation (league -2%) and keep firing even with a lead (43% early-down pass when ahead vs ~41%) — the kind of pass-first identity that keeps receivers live in every script.

The Offensive Blueprint

The WR2 is unusually involved here — 19% of targets (league ~15%), meaning there's bankable volume beyond the top receiver.

When they fall behind they abandon the run entirely — 60% pass while trailing, so their pass-catchers have huge comeback-script ceilings.

They push it downfield — average depth of target 8.6 yards with 22% of throws traveling 15+, a vertical passing game that trades completions for boom-or-bust yardage.

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they lean run-heavy, passing 48% of the time, funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — A Balanced Defense

Soft against opposing WR1s — 68 rec yds/game (vs ~58). A rec-yards target.

Soft against opposing WR2s — 44 rec yds/game (vs ~36). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 109 rushing and 252 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

They leak TE touchdowns (0.31/game vs ~0.24) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: their pass-catchers have massive ceilings in comeback scripts (fade-material as underdogs); opposing TE anytime-TD is a repeatable angle.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
